title: Remarks at Hotel Baltimore, Kansas City, Missouri
paragraphs: I wish to thank you most cordially not only for the beautiful token by which I shall always remember, if anything were necessary to make me remember, the pleasant lunch I have had with you to-day; but also I want to thank you for the distinguished kindness and hospitality with which I have been treated here. It is indeed a pleasure to come here. I am the eighth generation born in New York City of my people, so I think I am entitled to say that I am indeed in the heart of the country here; for I feel that here in what used to be the west, but now is so near the middle that I am sure it is not far from the effete east, is where our people develop those characteristics which we naturally associate with the name American. (Applause)

The west is so purely a relative term that you have to locate the man's individual abode before you know what he means by it. I remember that when I was in the cow country, one of the cow hands working for me came to me at the end of the season and said he would like his time as he was going away. I said " Where are you going?" He replied "I am going to spend the winter in the far east." "Well" I said" what do you mean by that, Norway or Nubia?" He said, "No, Duluth."
So to-day, in this country, we know no east or west, north or south, we merely know good Americans wherever.they may be. (Great applause)
